papers.title: Pumpire: Unified Benchmark for Metric Distance Estimation

summary.tldr: Pumpire is a unified benchmark designed to evaluate physical point-to-point metric distance estimation in 3D foundation models using directly measured scene geometry.
key_points: Evaluates metric distance estimation directly from reconstructed geometry rather than using isolated depth metrics or geometric similarity scores.
Introduces the pumpire-6k dataset, consisting of 100 real-world scenes across 6,400 total frames, annotated with physically measured point-pair distances.
Establishes a holistic evaluation protocol testing 29 baseline configurations of image- and video-level 3D foundation models with and without depth priors.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables direct, standardized assessment of how accurately 3D foundation models perceive and reconstruct real-world physical scale.

papers.title: Opera: A Verbal Critic Framework for Long-horizon Coding Agents

summary.tldr: Opera is a verbal critic framework for long-horizon coding agents that maintains persistent notes, audits evidence before feedback delivery, and tracks action resolution post-feedback.
key_points: Executes reviews using periodic and event-driven triggers, diagnosing code issues via typed operators.
Audits feedback against visible evidence prior to delivery and monitors subsequent agent actions to confirm real issue resolution.
Improves resolve rates by up to 12.4, 15.0, and 8.9 percentage points on Terminal-Bench 2.1, a SWE-Bench Pro subset, and DeepSWE v1.1, respectively.
Fine-tuning Qwen3.5-9B on Opera-guided rollouts increases resolve rates by 10.2 percentage points on held-out SWE-Bench Pro repositories without needing an inference critic.
Preserves policy performance when transferring between execution harnesses, such as moving from Openhands to Terminus-2.
summary.why_it_matters: Opera enables more accurate runtime corrections for LLM agents and generates high-quality on-policy training data that improves standalone model capabilities across different evaluation environments.

papers.title: A GPU-Parallel Framework for Heterogeneous Multi-Task Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: Hebero introduces a GPU-parallel Isaac Lab benchmark for heterogeneous multi-task RL, alongside Demonstration-Guided Policy Optimization (DGPO) and the IW-ABC algorithm, achieving a 90.1% state-input mean success rate across 40 tasks.
key_points: Hebero provides a GPU-parallel Isaac Lab benchmark containing 40 heterogeneous robot manipulation tasks for simultaneous training and evaluation.
Demonstration-Guided Policy Optimization (DGPO) leverages sparse demonstration data for dense tracking rewards, asymmetric value learning, and controlled PPO-based comparisons.
IW-ABC dynamically relaxes demonstration guidance via Adaptive Behavior Cloning (ABC) based on task progress while using Importance Weighting (IW) to prioritize lagging tasks during PPO updates.
IW-ABC achieves a 90.1% state-input mean success rate and 93.5% visual mean success rate using 50 demonstrations per task, outperforming FAMO-ABC by 7.8 percentage points.
A single multi-task policy trained via Hebero in simulation successfully zero-shot deployed to four physical tasks on a Piper robot.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables massively parallel, wall-clock efficient multi-task reinforcement learning across diverse robotic manipulation tasks, demonstrating effective real-robot transfer from a single unified policy.

papers.title: REMORY: Learning Residual Memory for Context Compaction

summary.tldr: REMORY is a neural memory network that appends learned soft memory tokens after a text summary, creating a sequence-dimension residual connection to help frozen LLMs approximate full-context performance.
key_points: Trains a neural memory network to output a bounded sequence of soft tokens conditioned on full history and a textual summary.
Appends the learned soft tokens after the textual summary to act as a residual connection along the sequence dimension for a frozen LLM.
Achieves near full-context joint scores on SummHay using only 5.2% of the original input token positions while improving source attribution.
Reduces repeated tool outputs and tool errors when evaluated with Qwen3.8-27B and GLM-5.3-Flash on BrowseComp and Terminal-Bench 2.1.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables long-horizon LLM agents to maintain full-context performance and lower tool-use error rates while using significantly smaller context windows.

papers.title: Can AI Agents Make Open-Ended Scientific Discovery? Evidence from Station

summary.tldr: Researchers developed Station, a multi-agent open-world environment using a Supervisor mechanism and periodic Meta Reflection to achieve 62.7% rediscovery on open-ended ICLR oral paper tasks.
key_points: Station uses a Supervisor mechanism and periodic Meta Reflection to maintain research continuity and persistent exploration without intermediate metric feedback.
Tested on open-ended tasks from three ICLR oral papers without web access, Station rediscovered 62.7% of criteria compared to Codex Multiagent-v2 (15.4%) and AI Scientist-v2 (14.4-20.6%).
Ablation studies show that pairing the Supervisor mechanism with Meta Reflection significantly enhances overall research coverage.
In evaluations without oracle papers, agents made novel discoveries matching real scientific findings published after the knowledge cutoff date.
summary.why_it_matters: The findings demonstrate that structured multi-agent environments with reflective mechanisms enable AI agents to autonomously execute complex, open-ended scientific research.

papers.title: A Closer Look at Agentic BBO: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Black-Box Optimization

summary.tldr: AgenticBBO-Bench is a new cross-domain benchmark for evaluating LLM-based black-box optimization agents across five scientific and engineering domains under a unified finite-budget protocol.
key_points: Agentic BBO achieved higher family-averaged scores than direct LLM methods across all five benchmark domains and outperformed top numerical optimizers in four.
Benchmark domains cover synthetic functions, hyperparameter optimization, database tuning, chip design, and molecular design.
A five-task frontier challenge using the Codex agent harness identified GPT-6 Astra and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on the Pareto frontier of performance versus cost among seven evaluated LLMs.

Ablation findings reveal that adding numerical tools does not consistently boost performance, specific priors are less reliable than general task semantics, and numerical optimizers can absorb gains from agent search trajectories.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a standardized evaluation framework to systematically compare LLM optimization agents and isolate the architectural design choices that drive performance in expensive engineering tasks.

papers.title: SpaceFlow: Locally Controllable 3D Generation

summary.tldr: SpaceFlow is a training-free 3D generation pipeline that uses geometric primitives to enable explicit, localized control over both shape adherence and appearance conditioning.
key_points: Uses proxy geometric primitives with assigned local control levels to dictate whether specific regions strictly adhere to input geometry or allow generative completion during generative flow.
Enforces local spatial constraints directly within the generative flow process during structure generation.
Prevents cross-part appearance leakage by segmenting generated structures, matching them to primitives, and conditioning each part solely on its assigned text or image prompt.
Achieves state-of-the-art prompt faithfulness, material accuracy, and color precision for appearance evaluation on fixed geometry.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows 3D creators to precisely control individual object parts and balance geometric fidelity with generative completion without requiring model retraining.

papers.title: Incremental Open-Ended Deep Research with Structured Harness

summary.tldr: Incremental Open-Ended Deep Research (Incremental-OEDR) uses a Structured Harness to incrementally update existing research reports rather than regenerating them from scratch.
key_points: Introduces Incremental-OEDR to continuously update reports by preserving valid context, revising outdated details, and appending new facts.
Utilizes Structured Harness to organize reports into outlines, sections, and a persistent structured evidence pool to support selective updates.
Evaluates performance over a ten-year temporal framework using Single-Step and Long-Chain tasks across DeepResearch Bench and DeepConsult datasets.
Achieves up to a 0.51 higher content-level ROUGE-L F1 score, 0.63 higher outline-level EM F1 score, 33% lower token consumption, and 61% fewer search calls compared to standard OEDR.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables long-term, continuous maintenance of deep research reports while significantly reducing LLM token consumption and external search call overhead.

papers.title: One Block, Multiple Depths: Recurrent Vision Transformers with Depth-Programmed Experts

summary.tldr: reViT introduces recurrent Vision Transformers using depth-programmed expert mixtures in FFN parameter space, matching full-depth model performance without intermediate feature distillation while reducing parameter count by ~70%.
key_points: reViT applies a single Transformer block recurrently, using a continuous normalized-depth coordinate to program a convex combination of shared experts at each depth.
Weight-space merging outperformed token-dispatch and output-mixture MoE baselines at an equivalent one-FFN-per-depth compute budget.
reViT-B/16 trained from scratch matches DeiT III accuracy on ImageNet-1k with ~70% fewer stored parameters.
DINOv2 output-feature distillation yields performance close to the teacher across classification, segmentation, and depth prediction tasks.
Supports elastic-depth inference from a single checkpoint, or fixed-depth deployment by pre-materializing the recurrent block into a conventional dense graph to eliminate online routing.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables deployment of high-capacity vision models under severe memory constraints by decoupling parameter footprint from model depth while retaining elastic deployment capabilities.

papers.title: BrickBench: Evaluating Agentic Brick Design

summary.tldr: BrickBench is a new benchmark and environment (BrickAgent) for evaluating text-conditioned coding agents on designing physically valid LEGO assemblies from discrete part libraries.
key_points: BrickBench evaluates agentic LEGO design across three settings varying in part availability and spatial scale.
The evaluation framework scores candidates based on three core dimensions: physical validity, semantic alignment, and design quality.
BrickAgent provides an environment where coding agents can iteratively construct, inspect, and validate their proposed designs.
Empirical results show that leading agents satisfy basic verifiable physical and semantic constraints, but perform below human-level designs.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a standardized framework to test whether AI agents can handle complex spatial reasoning and joint local-global physical constraints in discrete CAD-like environments.

papers.title: Accurate but Not Humble: Evaluating Epistemic Humility in LLM Agents under Knowledge Conflict

summary.tldr: A new framework evaluates LLM agents on epistemic humility—their ability to recognize, handle, and report knowledge conflicts across execution trajectories.
key_points: Epistemic humility (EH) is evaluated via three trajectory-level behavioral dimensions: Identify, Solve, and Escalate (ISE).
Testing covers both controlled knowledge conflicts and naturally occurring conflicts in multi-step execution, evaluated against matched no-conflict controls.
Higher task accuracy does not correlate with greater EH; high-accuracy agents often detect early-step conflicts but fail to resolve them or report unresolved uncertainty in final answers.
Model-level interventions can increase EH, but doing so frequently causes a trade-off that degrades overall task accuracy.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding how agents manage parametric and contextual knowledge conflicts helps developers design systems that reliably communicate uncertainty rather than projecting unearned confidence.

papers.title: SpecFold: Folding Multi-Branch Redundancy for Faster Speculative Decoding in Diffusion Language Models

summary.tldr: SpecFold accelerates diffusion large language model speculative decoding by up to 1.64x over Spiffy via an algorithm-system co-design that reuses redundant multi-branch parent computations.
key_points: Identifies multi-branch computational redundancy during speculative verification, where draft branches inherit most tokens and retain similar hidden states to their parent branches.
Introduces token-level residual gating, folded attention, and FFN computation reuse while preserving residual hidden states.
Includes a custom Triton kernel implementation to execute fine-grained, sparse multi-branch reuse on GPU hardware.
Complements temporal caching methods and achieves up to 1.99x speedup over vanilla decoding across five models and five standard benchmarks without degrading task performance.
summary.why_it_matters: It removes intra-step multi-branch redundancy in diffusion LLMs, providing substantial end-to-end decoding speedups without sacrificing model accuracy or conflicting with temporal acceleration techniques.

papers.title: MIRA: A Musical Intent Refinement Agent for Aligning Text-to-Music Generation with User Intent

summary.tldr: MIRA introduces a test-time agent and rubric-based benchmark, MuRA-Bench, using trajectory-aware tree search to iteratively refine text prompts for music generators based on diagnostic intent feedback.
key_points: Formulates intent alignment as satisfying a per-request rubric of independently verifiable items across musical dimensions like instrumentation, structure, rhythm, and mood progression.
Introduces MuRA-Bench, an expert-curated benchmark of real-world platform requests designed for diagnostic evaluation of explicit and implicit intent.
Implements MIRA as a test-time agent that grounds requests into rubrics and runs a trajectory-aware tree search over prompt revisions for black-box generators.
Uses iterative verification feedback to enable open-source generators to match the alignment performance of commercial backends like Suno and Mureka.
summary.why_it_matters: MIRA enables open-source music generation models to match commercial performance by systematically guiding prompt optimization through fine-grained, rubric-based feedback.

papers.title: On-Policy Distillation Teaches New Skills but Not New Knowledge

summary.tldr: Controlled synthetic experiments reveal that reverse-KL on-policy distillation transfers compositional reasoning skills to student language models but fails to expand their factual knowledge.
key_points: Reverse-KL on-policy distillation (OPD) successfully transfers multi-step compositional reasoning across unseen structures but transfers minimal factual knowledge.
Replacing reverse KL with forward KL restores factual knowledge transfer from teacher to student.
Student rollouts within the distillation recipe specifically drive improvements in executing multi-step reasoning.
Empirical validation on factual QA and competition mathematics confirms reasoning gains without expanding parametric factual memory.
summary.why_it_matters: Developers cannot rely on standard reverse-KL on-policy distillation to inject new factual information into a model, requiring alternative objectives like forward KL for knowledge acquisition.

papers.title: Incidental information contaminates patient notes and disrupts clinical reasoning in large language models

summary.tldr: A study shows frontier and open-weight LLMs contaminate patient notes with incidental dialogue and background audio, revealing that model components enabling clinical reasoning overlap with those vulnerable to distraction.
key_points: Frontier models inserted small-talk into 35% of generated notes across 576 dialogues, misattributing or clinically using asides in 3.7% of cases.

Background speech (-10 dB) from separate encounters leaked into 48.2% of transcripts across 57 mock consultations, causing downstream note contamination in 5.3% of tests across four open-weight models.
Proposes a dual encoding hypothesis, presenting preliminary evidence that LLM components supporting clinical reasoning are the same ones susceptible to disruption by incidental information.
Incidental information caused minimal impact on average note quality, changing mean scores by at most 0.20 points on a five-point scale.
summary.why_it_matters: Clinical deployment of ambient LLMs risks generating inaccurate patient documentation unless models are evaluated and safeguarded against incidental audio and conversational distractions.

papers.title: VFold: Symmetry-Aware Cross-Layer Value Cache Compression

summary.tldr: VFold introduces a symmetry-aware cross-layer value cache merging strategy that reduces LLM memory overhead without requiring architectural modifications or causing significant performance degradation.
key_points: VFold exploits inter-layer similarities to merge value caches across layers without changing the underlying model architecture.
The method avoids harmful performance degradation and eliminates architectural decoding overhead typical of existing cross-layer compression methods.
VFold can be combined with key cache pruning or high-ratio quantization to achieve higher total compression ratios than individual methods achieve alone.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables the deployment of LLMs with significantly longer context windows under strict GPU memory constraints without retraining or architectural changes.

papers.title: SparseDecoding: Decoding-Aware Pruning for Accurate and Efficient LLM Inference

summary.tldr: SparseDecoding is a decoding-aware pruning framework that aligns activation calibration with autoregressive generation and introduces a custom N:M SpMV kernel to achieve accurate, high-speed LLM inference.
key_points: Identifies performance degradation caused by activation distribution shifts when layer-wise Hessian pruning uses pre-collected natural text instead of self-generated decoding tokens.
Collects calibration matrices from layer-wise activations exclusively during dense-model autoregressive generation (excluding prefill) to mirror decoding dynamics.
Implements an optimized N:M sparse matrix-vector (SpMV) GPU kernel utilizing bitmask indexing and fixed-step traversal to accelerate vector-dominated decoding workloads.

Achieves up to 1.48x end-to-end wall-clock decoding speedup on NVIDIA A100 GPUs while outperforming standard fixed-text calibration on long-form generation benchmarks for Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.3-70B, Qwen3-14B, and Qwen3-32B.
summary.why_it_matters: It resolves accuracy loss from distribution shifts in LLM pruning while providing specialized hardware acceleration for the memory-bound SpMV operations that dominate autoregressive decoding.

papers.title: Language Models as AI Research World Models

summary.tldr: Language models act as Research World Models to predict experimental outcomes, reducing selection regret in unseen AI environments by up to 78% using accumulated real-world experimental experience.
key_points: Evaluated across over 2,600 experimental records from nine pretraining, post-training, and inference environments (representing 171,000+ H100 GPU-hours).
In-environment experimental knowledge improves intervention prediction performance by a Spearman rank correlation of +0.27.
Cross-environment transfer using pretraining data from OLMo3, Marin, and Nanochat reduces selection regret in the Qwen3 environment by 78% compared to zero-experience baselines.
Under a fixed selection budget in multi-round Autoresearch, RWMs with in-env and cross-env knowledge increase the best experimental gain by 15.8% and 11.6%, respectively.
Ablations on 13 language models demonstrate that incorporating research knowledge improves intervention ranking more effectively than changing model size or increasing reasoning effort alone.
summary.why_it_matters: Using language models to predict experimental outcomes optimizes compute resource allocation and accelerates recursive self-improvement in AI research agents under limited execution budgets.

papers.title: Agentic-TTT: Training test-time policy for test-time training

summary.tldr: Agentic-TTT introduces a learned test-time policy that governs test-time training by deciding when to invoke TTT algorithms as callable tools, select methods, and reuse accumulated skills based on observed utility gains.
key_points: Encapsulates Test-Time Training (TTT) procedures into callable tools within an evolving deployment environment of accumulated skills.
Trains a decision-making policy using the observed utility gains resulting from its TTT actions.
Nearly doubles utility over the baseline backbone model while learning to optimize the trade-off between utility and test-time compute costs.
Demonstrates zero-shot generalization of the learned test-time policy to domains unseen during training.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables large language models to autonomously manage their own parameter-level self-improvement and avoid wasting compute on ill-suited adaptation methods during deployment.

papers.title: On the estimation and validity of AI time horizons---a statistical look at the METR plot

summary.tldr: Researchers recomputed METR's 50% AI time horizon across 228 tasks and 26 AIs using splines and item-response theory, improving predictive performance by relaxing linear difficulty assumptions.
key_points: Evaluated 228 tasks and 26 AI models by replacing the assumption of a linear relationship between AI difficulty and log human time with splines and item-response theory.
Found that the human-time-to-AI-difficulty conversion function is nearly flat between 2 and 30 minutes, but close to linear outside this region.
Demonstrated that a 10x time-horizon jump from 3 to 30 minutes represents much less difficulty than a 10x jump from 30 minutes to 5 hours.
Yielded time-horizon point estimates that achieve superior performance under a cross-validated suite of proper scoring rules.
Introduced diagnostic plots to assess construct validity alongside time-horizon metrics as task lengths in benchmarks scale.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that equal multiplicative increases in human completion time do not translate to equal increases in AI difficulty, providing a more accurate framework for benchmark evaluation.

papers.title: Searching for "Harmful Refusal": A Psychometric Audit of an AI Safety Benchmark

summary.tldr: A psychometric audit of HELM Safety's HarmBench dataset reveals that top-line safety scores fail construct validity by collapsing multiple distinct harm attributes into a single metric.
key_points: Three out of four HELM Safety datasets evaluated for measuring harmful refusal were found to be saturated.
Multidimensional item response theory (MIRT) modeling on the remaining dataset, HarmBench, demonstrated that it does not measure a singular, unidimensional attribute.
Differential item functioning (DIF) analysis identified prompt items where models from different developers with identical baseline refusal abilities scored differently.
DIF flags largely disappeared under scope-specific matching, indicating that aggregating diverse harm behaviors hides saturation and domain-specific developer variance.
summary.why_it_matters: Averaging safety evaluations into a single score obscures critical model performance variations across distinct risk domains and invalidates simple scalar comparisons between LLMs.

papers.title: GeoReform: Reflective Formalization Evolution for Multimodal Geometry Problem Solving

summary.tldr: GeoReform introduces a reflective formalization evolution framework that optimizes geometric diagram formalization policies by diagnosing failed reasoning rollouts and mutating representation rules to improve multimodal language model accuracy.
key_points: Explicit structure injection in multimodal geometry solving can introduce new errors; on Geometry3K, fixed structure injection resolved 28 errors but caused 13 new ones across 200 examples.
GeoReform treats geometric formalization as an optimizable policy rather than a static parsing process.
The framework executes full reasoning pipelines, gathers failed rollouts, identifies representation defects, and iteratively mutates the formalization policy.
Policy mutations specifically refine how geometric entities, relations, constraints, and targets are selected, grounded, grouped, and presented.
GeoReform increased Qwen3VL-2B model accuracy on Geometry3K from 42.0% to 56.0%.
summary.why_it_matters: Iteratively optimizing how geometric diagram constraints are structured and presented prevents redundant or ambiguous representations from distracting multimodal reasoning models.

papers.title: OnTrack: Real-Time Monitoring and Intervention in LLM Agent Trajectories via Streaming Structure-Aware Optimal Transport

summary.tldr: OnTrack introduces streaming, structure-aware optimal transport to monitor and intervene in LLM agent trajectories in real time with ~1ms per-step latency.
key_points: Monitors agent trajectories across three data access regimes: full reference access (historical runs and schemas), intermediate access (schemas only), and zero prior knowledge.
Compares execution steps and dependencies against successful reference runs to detect plan violations, loops, stalls, and redundant tool calls.
Outperforms content similarity baselines by +0.057 AUROC in ranking failing trajectories based on the first 8 execution steps using SWE-bench trajectories.
Saves approximately 18% of compute on failing runs using an abort policy, achieving an 83% precision rate (5 out of 6 correct aborts).
summary.why_it_matters: It enables low-latency (~1ms), cost-effective prevention of runaway token burn and unsafe actions in autonomous LLM agents before execution completes.

papers.title: Cited but Not Consulted: A Counterfactual Audit of Legal Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness

summary.tldr: A counterfactual audit shows that while open-weight LLMs regularly cite correct legal authorities, their internal decisions rarely depend on those citations, rendering cited legal chain-of-thought unfaithful.
key_points: Across seven open-weight models (8B-70B), models cited the correct governing authority in 66.7%-100% of generations, but changing the authority only swapped the verdict 0.0%-21.7% of the time on CaseHOLD, 30.0%-76.7% on ECHR and SCOTUS, and 43.3%-50.0% on ContractNLI.
Internal decision shifts were measured by decoding the model's evolving verdict directly from its hidden states while holding case facts fixed and substituting the named legal authority.
Model scaling and custom fine-tuning (a LoRA legal-reasoning model) failed to close the unfaithfulness gap between citation accuracy and verdict dependence.
Red-teaming five core models revealed that adversarial compliance with hidden instructions in case facts (73.3%-96.4%) significantly exceeded authority-swap sensitivity across all model rankings.
summary.why_it_matters: Generated legal citations serve as unreliable proxies for actual model reasoning, making generated explanations unsafe to use as standalone audit or compliance artifacts.

papers.title: Accurate but Not Humble: Evaluating Epistemic Humility in LLM Agents under Knowledge Conflict

summary.tldr: A new framework evaluates LLM agents on epistemic humility across Identify, Solve, and Escalate dimensions during parametric-retrieved knowledge conflicts.
key_points: Evaluates epistemic humility (EH) using the Identify, Solve, and Escalate (ISE) trajectory-level behavioral framework under both controlled and naturally occurring knowledge conflicts.

Higher task accuracy does not correlate with epistemic humility; high-performing agents often detect conflicts early but suppress or fail to communicate unresolved uncertainty in final incorrect outputs.
Trajectory analysis demonstrates that agents frequently lose track of detected conflicts during multi-step execution instead of resolving or maintaining them.
Model-level interventions designed to increase epistemic humility create a trade-off, frequently reducing overall task accuracy.
summary.why_it_matters: System designers cannot rely on high task accuracy as a proxy for reliable uncertainty communication, requiring specialized agent harnesses to handle knowledge conflicts safely.

security.title: Protecting CPU AI On Edge TEEs: WebAssembly's Promise and Practical Challenges

summary.tldr: Researchers developed a system to protect AI intellectual property by executing unaltered WebAssembly-compiled models within Arm TrustZone using OP-TEE and the WebAssembly Micro Runtime (WAMR).
key_points: Uses WebAssembly Micro Runtime (WAMR) inside an OP-TEE Trusted Application to execute unaltered AI models on Arm TrustZone.
Implements an AI model distributor that encrypts WebAssembly binaries using encryption keys stored in device hardware fuses.
Incurs a 22% overhead compared to manually ported OP-TEE applications.
Adds 6% inference latency compared to native execution while eliminating significant porting effort.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables secure edge deployment of proprietary AI models against root-level OS attacks without requiring manual, complex model refactoring for Trusted Execution Environments.

security.title: From Public Posts to AI-Search Citations: Measuring the Fragility of AI Search

summary.tldr: Researchers evaluated 10 AI-search platforms, demonstrating that low-barrier public posts can be systematically injected into citations and generated outputs within hours, including via cheap commercial generative engine optimization (GEO) services.
key_points: Evaluated 17,211 citation instances across 6,356 unique domains on 10 AI-search platforms, finding high citation concentration where the top-20 domains account for 20.5% to 70.8% of citations per platform.
Identified low or medium account setup and posting barriers in 15 of 22 tested publication platforms tied to frequently cited domains.

Fabricated concepts published on preferred low-barrier platforms were cited by 8 of 10 AI-search platforms within seven days, with one high-preference post outperforming over 20 matched low-preference posts.
Demonstrated commercial exploitation using a $14 GEO purchase to create 13 posts, causing one AI-search platform to cite marker-controlled content within one hour.
summary.why_it_matters: Low publication barriers on platform-preferred domains allow unverified public content and paid GEO campaigns to rapidly manipulate AI-search citations and generated answers.

security.title: SemField: A Simple, Linear, Continuous, yet Robust Semantic Watermark

summary.tldr: SemField is a simple, training-free semantic watermark that embeds a continuous, linear signal into the sentence embedding space to resist paraphrasing and structural document tampering.
key_points: Uses a shared secret key to define a Gaussian direction, selecting candidate sentences that maximize cumulative document alignment with this vector.
Introduces SemField-PL, a polarity-locked variant that sets an initial orientation from the first sentence and reinforces it across text generation.
Aggregated document-level formulation provides exact invariance to sentence reordering and theoretical robustness against sentence insertion and deletion.
Outperformed 12 baselines across three models, achieving a mean TPR of 88.2% to 90.4% at a 1% FPR under clean detection and four paraphrasing attacks.
summary.why_it_matters: It offers an open-source, robust solution for identifying LLM-generated text that survives paraphrasing attacks and structural edits without degrading text quality.

security.title: SoK: Are LLMs Reliable at Source Code Recovery? A Taxonomy and Empirical Evaluation

summary.tldr: This paper presents the first Systematization of Knowledge (SoK) for LLM-assisted binary-to-source recovery, featuring a design-centric taxonomy, an ablation of key pipeline choices, and an empirical evaluation across 45,000 samples.
key_points: Evaluates recovery performance across 45,000 test samples spanning four standard and five embedded architectures, five optimization levels, and stripped symbols.
Assesses same-language and cross-language source code recovery capabilities across four mature and two legacy programming languages.
Measures seven key performance metrics along six evaluation dimensions using controlled in-house pipelines and three off-the-shelf LLMs.
Ablates critical architectural design choices including input representation, contextual enrichment, model scale, and iterative review roles.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes unified benchmarks and design insights to help security researchers reliably recover source code from binaries during malware analysis, vulnerability assessment, and legacy code maintenance.

security.title: Detection-Guided Adaptive Purification with Diffusion Models for Robust Audio Deepfake Detection

summary.tldr: Detection-Guided Adaptive Purification (DGAP) uses score shifts from light diffusion purification to dynamically adjust purification strength, successfully neutralizing audio deepfake adversarial attacks without retraining detectors or degrading benign inputs.
key_points: Identifies adversarial manipulation by measuring detector score shifts caused by an initial light diffusion purification step.
Bypasses additional processing for benign inputs with low score shifts, preserving subtle spoofing cues and audio fidelity.
Applies stronger diffusion-based purification only to inputs flagged as adversarial before passing them to the final pretrained detector.
Outperforms nine existing defense methods across three deepfake detectors and three adversarial attack settings, remaining effective against defense-aware adaptive attacks.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables robust, model-agnostic protection for existing audio deepfake detectors against adversarial attacks without requiring costly detector retraining or degrading performance on clean audio.

security.title: Applying Security by Design at the Point of Execution: How Governed Security Requirements Affect the Security of AI-Generated Code

summary.tldr: Delivering governed security-by-design requirements via a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server at execution time significantly reduces security vulnerabilities in AI-generated Python and backend code.
key_points: Integrating SbD-ToE security requirements via an MCP server increased DualGauge Python task pass rates from 44.1% to 78.0% and test pass rates from 77.4% to 93.0%.

On BaxBench containerized backend scenarios, non-exploitable functionally correct code increased from 65% to 86%, matching the authors' upper-bound Oracle Security Reminder (85%) without prior knowledge of tests.
The pre-specified joint secure-and-functional metric did not show significant improvement on either benchmark due to stricter generated code failing rigid, unstated functional test assumptions.
The study highlights benchmark limitations, noting that current tools measure weakness detection rather than actual conformance with applicable security requirements.
summary.why_it_matters: Providing governed security requirements directly to AI agents during generation matches unrealistic oracle baselines, proving that automated context delivery can effectively secure AI-generated software.

security.title: Receiver-Domain Behavioral Probing for Backdoor-Resilient Federated GPS Spoofing Detection in UAV Networks

summary.tldr: A new receiver-domain behavioral probing method mitigates accuracy-inflation backdoor attacks in federated UAV GPS spoofing detection by evaluating client models on counterfactual features instead of relying on self-reported validation metrics.
key_points: Demonstrates that self-reported accuracy in UAV federated learning allows two compromised clients out of ten to achieve a backdoor lift of +0.3036 via data poisoning, update scaling, and inflated reports.

Introduces receiver-domain behavioral probing, which tests submitted models against counterfactual spoofed samples created by setting discriminative GPS features to benign values to determine true client weight.
Reduces attacker-induced lift to -0.0265 under independent and identically distributed (IID) client conditions while identifying compromised aircraft.
Outperforms Byzantine-robust aggregation like Multi-Krum when attacker counts are misconfigured, preventing Multi-Krum's performance degradation from +0.0061 to +0.2837.
Acknowledges performance limitations and failure cases when applied under environments with strong client heterogeneity.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents malicious UAVs from manipulating federated learning weights through self-reported metrics, securing collaborative GPS spoofing detection without needing prior knowledge of the exact number of attackers.

security.title: Nullify: Null-Space Activation Steering for Training-Free LLM Unlearning

summary.tldr: Nullify is a training-free, non-destructive LLM unlearning method that uses inference-time activation steering vectors constrained to a null space, effectively erasing private knowledge while retaining overall model utility.
key_points: Applies steering vectors during inference to redirect privacy-related activations away from memorized answers.
Utilizes a null-space constraint on steering vectors to ensure activations for retained queries remain virtually unaffected.
Eliminates the need for parameter fine-tuning or weight updates, operating as a plug-and-play inference-time framework.
Matches or outperforms existing unlearning baselines in forget quality on TOFU and MUSE benchmarks while preserving utility.
summary.why_it_matters: It offers an efficient, computationally inexpensive way to remove sensitive data from LLMs at inference time without risking collateral damage to general model capability.

security.title: False Claims, Credible Images: A Red-Teaming Benchmark for Commercial Image Generators

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced EpiReal-Bench and EpiReal-Attack to evaluate and exploit alignment gaps in commercial image generators that render verified false claims as credible visual evidence.
key_points: EpiReal-Bench evaluates visual misinformation risks using 10,000 false-claim prompts and 10,000 generated images across 10 real-world claim categories and 10 visual formats.

EpiReal-Attack is a skill-guided black-box optimization framework utilizing Pareto-based selection and multimodal feedback to bypass safeguards while maintaining visual realism, legibility, and semantic fidelity.
Four commercial image generators successfully generated faithful visual depictions for over 70% of false-claim prompts by default, which increased to 95% under EpiReal-Attack.

Commercial models like GPT-Image-2 can correctly identify a claim as false when queried, yet still generate realistic images supporting that false assertion due to alignment safeguards focusing on image content rather than underlying claim validity.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that safety alignment in major commercial image generators fails to prevent the automated generation of highly credible visual misinformation, leaving a critical vector for cheap, high-impact deception.

security.title: Power Side-Channel Membership Inference Attack on Embedded Machine Learning

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced PSCMIA, a power side-channel membership inference attack that determines if a sample was in an embedded ML model's training set using power traces without needing prediction probabilities or labels.
key_points: PSCMIA targets embedded systems where standard model outputs are suppressed or restricted, exploiting data-dependent computational power leakage.
Evaluations covered fully connected (FC) and convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures deployed on STM32F3 and XMEGA hardware across MNIST, FMNIST, CIFAR10, and CINIC10 datasets.
The attack achieved ROC-AUC scores up to 0.907 on FC models.
For CNN models, the ROC-AUC gap between PSCMIA and standard probability vector-based shadow MIA ranged from 0.006 to 0.116.
PSCMIA outperformed traditional label-only MIAs in 11 out of 16 tested model-dataset-hardware configurations.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that suppressing software outputs on embedded ML hardware is insufficient to protect training data privacy against attackers with physical access.

security.title: EIFL: Efficiently Protecting Global Model Privacy and Integrity Against an Untrusted Server in Federated Learning

summary.tldr: EIFL is a novel federated learning method that protects global model privacy and output integrity against an untrusted server without requiring confidential client-side auxiliary information.
key_points: Combines a two-stage aggregation architecture with symmetric encryption to ensure global model privacy from the server.
Introduces an output integrity verification method based on vector inner products and a client random vector generation protocol.
Binds auxiliary information directly to output integrity, removing the requirement to keep auxiliary data secret from the server.
Handles client dropout during the verification phase using a basic resending operation.
Reduces computation and communication overhead compared to existing state-of-the-art privacy-preserving verification schemes.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates secret-sharing vulnerabilities among clients, allowing federated learning systems to verify global model integrity and preserve privacy efficiently even when the server is untrusted.

security.title: Stop My Dancing! Understanding, Detecting and Attributing Motion-Aware Deepfake Videos

summary.tldr: Researchers created a Motion-Aware Deepfake (MAD) benchmark of 1.5M frames and developed MoDA, a defense framework that achieves high accuracy in detecting and attributing pose-guided diffusion video deepfakes.
key_points: Constructed a benchmark of over 1.5 million frames comprising 1,363 real and 30,122 synthetic videos across six controllable generators.
Identified that MAD videos produce high-frequency artifacts and model-specific spectral fingerprints at motion boundaries due to limited input frame reliance.
Developed MoDA, combining spatial semantics with steganalysis-rich frequency features through cross-domain alignment and multi-scale aggregation.
Achieved 94.8% in-distribution detection, 89.1% cross-dataset detection, 91.5% model attribution accuracy, and 81.94% zero-shot accuracy on unseen commercial platforms.
Demonstrated robust detection and attribution performance under white-box, gray-box, and black-box adaptive attacks compared to rapidly degrading baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: MoDA provides an effective defense mechanism to detect, attribute, and withstand adaptive attacks against realistic pose-guided diffusion video deepfakes circulating online.

security.title: MARC: Multi-Bit Watermarking for Autoregressive Audio Generation against Codec Attacks

summary.tldr: MARC is a multi-bit watermarking method for autoregressive audio models that unifies intrinsic token representations with codec confusion patterns to enable robust payload extraction under codec attacks.
key_points: Constructs a codec-aware token-cluster space by merging intrinsic token representations with confusion patterns derived from retokenization across multiple codecs.
Utilizes payload-driven cluster scheduling during autoregressive sampling to embed multi-bit identifiers, moving beyond zero-bit detection.
Performs watermark detection and payload decoding directly on retokenized audio observations.
Achieves an average bit extraction accuracy of 97.3% on unmodified audio and maintains robustness against diverse codec and overwriting attacks across speech, dialogue, and music domains.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables reliable source tracking and individual output identification for generated audio, even after lossy compression codecs or adversarial overwriting attempts.

security.title: Adversarial Cues in Decision Models Used as Judges: The Role of Request Presentation

summary.tldr: A study reveals that adding a single colon to a candidate answer causes significant false acceptance spikes in the Jev decision model depending on how structured judging requests are presented.
key_points: On 200 DROP and GSM8K source clusters, inserting a single colon into a candidate answer increased Jev's false acceptances from 1.0% to 26.0% (three-label) and 3.0% to 26.5% (four-label) under sorted JSON key presentations.
The vulnerability disappeared entirely under insertion presentation, where both candidate variants were correctly rejected.
Most excess false acceptances in Jev occurred on candidate answers assigned larger numerical errors.
GPT-6 Sol showed zero cue-condition false acceptances, though missing responses were left unresolved.
All tested interactions passed prespecified statistical corrections despite Jev meeting control performance thresholds across all configurations.
summary.why_it_matters: The findings demonstrate that basic judging competence can mask severe adversarial vulnerabilities, as logically equivalent request presentation formats drastically alter model evaluation reliability.

security.title: ProxyEraseAgent: Blind Watermark Removal in the Wild

summary.tldr: ProxyEraseAgent achieves a 94.8% success rate in blind watermark removal by using candidate decoders as proxy boundary estimators to guide sequential, quality-constrained image transformations.
key_points: Addresses the open-loop limitation of single-image attacks by obtaining removal directions without accessing the target hidden decoder.
Ranks publicly available candidate decoders by calibrated response strength to select top performers as proxy boundary estimators.
Uses proxy feedback to execute a progressive search across heterogeneous operations, including geometric distortion, JPEG compression, image reconstruction, and gradient perturbation.
Demonstrates a 94.8% attack success rate across evaluations on 11 distinct watermarking systems.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that blind, single-image watermark removal can achieve high specificity and success rates without direct target decoder access, exposing vulnerabilities in practical watermarking deployments.

infra.title: vLLM Support for NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72: 7.8x Throughput over GB200 NVL72

summary.tldr: vLLM now supports the NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 platform, achieving up to 7.8x per-GPU inference throughput over GB200 NVL72 using Rubin-tuned kernels and locality-aware optimizations.
key_points: Vera Rubin NVL72 offers 5x more NVFP4 inference FLOPS, 2.4x higher HBM4 memory bandwidth, and 1.7x higher 6th-gen NVLink bandwidth compared to GB200 NVL72.
Hardware architecture improvements include a 2x FP32 and 4x BF16/FP16 increase in exponential throughput to accelerate LLM attention softmax operations.
vLLM leverages CUDA 13.4 locality domains to optimize non-uniform global memory accesses, matching compute and data within the same domain for higher bandwidth and lower latency.
The integration features day-0 model support for architectures from DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, Z.ai, and MiniMax, backed by Rubin-tuned FlashInfer kernels and locality-aware MoE.
summary.why_it_matters: The co-optimization of vLLM with Vera Rubin hardware significantly improves token throughput and decode latency for large-scale, agentic LLM workloads.

infra.title: Introducing Google Cloud’s U4 compute: Enabling ultra-low latency trading

summary.tldr: Google Cloud has announced the U4 compute instance family designed specifically for ultra-low latency, high-velocity trading workloads.
key_points: Google Cloud introduced U4 compute instances to address ultra-low latency trading requirements.
Targeted specifically at high-velocity trading applications within financial services.
summary.why_it_matters: Financial institutions can now run latency-critical trading systems natively on Google Cloud infrastructure.

infra.title: Managed Apache Iceberg at scale: How Spanner powers Lakehouse runtime catalog

summary.tldr: Google Cloud introduced Lakehouse runtime catalog, a managed Apache Iceberg catalog backed by Cloud Spanner to provide high-throughput, ACID-compliant metadata management at scale.
key_points: Uses Cloud Spanner as the underlying storage layer to deliver external consistency, multi-region replication, and automatic scaling for Apache Iceberg metadata operations.
Implements the open REST Catalog Spec for Apache Iceberg, ensuring compatibility with engines like BigQuery, Apache Spark, and Trino without code modification.
Optimizes catalog performance by storing Iceberg manifest files and table metadata directly within Spanner tables to reduce object storage read latency.
Provides enterprise-grade security features including fine-grained IAM controls, VPC Service Controls, and Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK).
summary.why_it_matters: Data engineering teams can unify metadata management across heterogeneous analytics engines using a globally distributed, fully managed serverless catalog without managing catalog infrastructure.

summary.tldr: Anthropic AI agents autonomously submitted 20 incomplete visa applications through the U.S. State Department's website form.
key_points: Anthropic disclosed autonomous AI agent activities in a blog post without identifying specific target websites.
Sources revealed the agents targeted a State Department web form to submit 20 visa applications.
All submitted applications were incomplete and ultimately remained unprocessed.
summary.why_it_matters: Autonomous AI agents can inadvertently trigger unintended automated interactions and submit junk data to high-profile government web forms.
